chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: T. Holder and the two Twelve Clouds of Joy
summary: Bandleader T. Holder had run off with the original Twelve Clouds of Joy's money, so Andy Kirk got that band while Holder used the name again in Dallas.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy
Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: In other words, we were auditioning. So all of us passed, and we formed this band. Now the band leader was named T. Holder. Now T. Holder was one of the very sharp, good, beautiful trumpet players that had been with Alphonso Trent over the years, and the reason T. Holder was in Dallas is because T. Holder had formed the Twelve Clouds of Joy; Kirk was the bass player, and he had John Williams, Mary Lou Williams first husband in on the saxophone, and in other words, he had formed the Twelve Clouds of Joy, and they were working in Tulsa.
T. Holder had run away with the money and came back
to Dallas, and they had fired T. Holder and wouldn't let him come back, and they put Andy Kirk Clerk in charge, and that's how it became Andy Kirk Clerk and his Twelve -- (Clouds of Joy)
(End of proceedings as recorded.)
SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTION
Interview with Albert "Budd" Johnson
Tape Two
Washington, D. C.

PROCEEDINGS Kirk
SO that's how Andy Clerk gets the Clouds of Joy, that's most interesting.
That's right.
I never heard this before.

So they let Andy take the band over because he was the most logical man. He had finished from the University, he had gone down to the university what is it, in Nashville, Tennessee? What is that, the -- not Meharry, that's the -- [Fisk]
No, that's the medical school.

That's the (inaudible) in Nashville. My recollection of -- but I mean he was a college man, and they figured that by him being a college man he was qualified to handle the band, so they put it in his hands, and you know he played bass.
Bass, right.

And he played a little saxaphone too. But anyway, getting back to the first black nightclub, well we had -- we were fortunate enough to get hold of a man by the name of Eddie Thompkins on trumpet, who later played with Jimmy Lunceford and was an outstanding trumpet player, and the rest of the guys --
Now what band is this, Budd?
This was the -- T. Holder's Twelve
Clouds of Joy.
T. Holder, you were in that?
He still -- yes. Me, my brother Keg, and --
T. Holder -- you were in T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy.
Yeah, because that's after he had left Andy Kirk and escaped with the money, and then he came, but it was his band name, so he used it with us, Twelve Clouds of Joy.
Well he took Eleven Clouds of Joy. Andy made one, and he had another one.
That's right. Well he had the first one. But he stole the money and left, and ran away, and everything, so they put the band, and they kept the name Twelve Clouds of Joy, but so did he.
So did Andy Kirk.
So did T. Holder.
So did T. Holder.
Because he --
I see.
-- originated the name.
So one was the Twelve Clouds of Joy and one was Andy Kirk and the Twelve Clouds of Joy.
That's right, which was later, because

T. Holder -- you see, T. Holder was the first Twelve Clouds of Joy, but he ran away with the money, and left the guys there in Tulsa on the job, and so they fired him, wouldn't take him back, and they remained the Twelve Clouds of Joy, because then they turned the band over to Andy Kirk.

But when T. Holder came to Dallas, and went into this first black nightclub, he said the Twelve Clouds of Joy, because it was his name, you know what I mean? Twelve Clouds of Joy. I don't know whether he was doing business as this name, or whether it was incorporated, or not. But he felt that it was his.
